# Queue

Every open item in rcad, one row each, in five tiers. `docs/decisions.md` §230
is the argument for the shape and the grammar below. The dispatcher edits this
file — to `lane:` when it dispatches a row, to `done:` when it merges one — and
a lane never writes it, so no two lanes conflict over it.

A row is one line inside a fenced block under its tier's heading, as `<id>
<tier> <state> <model> <write set> <what>`, the fields split by spaces. The
shape is only described here, never fenced: `just check-queue` reads every
fenced line as a row, so a fenced template would be a row nobody ranked.

- **id** — `T<n>`, `D<n>` or `Q<n>`, unique in the file. `T` and `D` numbers are
  carried over from the retired `docs/test-plan.md`.
- **tier** — `1`, `2`, `2.5`, `3` or `4` (§230.1).
- **state** — `todo`; `lane:<branch>`; `after:<id>[,<id>]`; `done:<sha>`;
  `dropped:§N`; or `parked:§N`.
- **model** — `opus` or `sonnet`; `-` only on a closed row that never recorded one.
- **write set** — comma-separated paths, directories (ending `/`), or
  `path#item`; `-` means the lane writes no tracked file but a new section of
  its own.
- **what** — ends in at least one `§N`/`§N.M`; on a `done` row the last one is
  the section that records the result.

A row is **ready** when its state is `todo`, or `after:` names only `done` rows.

Q549 1    done:5d4e60e63eed58a1b17c8fb20dacefacb81d0b28    opus    crates/rcad-topo/src/measure.rs,crates/rcad-topo/tests/a_flat_solid_publishes_the_rounding_of_its_measure.rs   wrong/D The centroid_wobble a flat solid and each flat face publish (§338.5) rests on exact sums that assume nothing underflows, one factor deeper than the volume and area sums of Q402: the solid moment is a determinant times a fourth offset, a face weight is two cross products and its moment takes a fifth side, and the measured middle offset from the hub or apex is scaled down by the axis shift. A gap: the ruling at the arc's middle angle, cut by the plane, gives a point 0 or 4.4e-16 off both surfaces. In walk.rs, for a plane-cone conic far larger than the run's ends, work off the arc rather than the conic: place points by angle round the cone (along the ruling at angle a the distance is -s0/(s1-s0)), pick the stretch (picked_by_all) at that point, charge the deviation by the arc's size, and count steps (how_many_steps, whose acos(1 - room/reach) rounds to 0 below room 1.35) by the arc's bend. In mesh.rs, bound the floor (how_far_the_points_of_reach, how_far_along_its_axis_this_face_runs) by the arc, not the whole conic. Q1058's probe of the points alone moved four of the six to answers that validate and hold the grid but cannot be measured (floor 2.2e4), and two to 'area swept by a wire round a normal'. Q1530 1    done:58532e26    opus    tooling/queue/,tooling/queue-page/render.py,justfile#queue,justfile#_queue-rows,justfile#check-queue-selftest,justfile#check-queue-api-selftest,.claude/agents/lane.md,docs/decisions.d/424-a-lane-narrows-its-hold-once-it-knows-where-it-works.md   pinned/1 A lane narrows its hold once it knows where it works (§424.3). Add just queue narrow <id> <write set>: under the claims lock it appends narrow <id> <time> <worktree> <write set> to the claims file and writes no docs/queue.md, so a lane may run it from its own tree. Refuse an id nobody holds; an entry outside the write set the row was taken with (a directory holds the paths under it, a file holds its items); and a widening back, to an entry inside the taken set but outside the current one, when that entry meets another running hold. Claims.holds() takes the last narrow as the hold's write set, and next, blocked, running, elsewhere and the queue page read it, for this copy's own lane: rows as well as rows held elsewhere; release clears it. In lane.md, a writing lane narrows at its first edit under src/ to the files or items it now knows it will change, and again before it reports, to the files its branch changed; a bundle lane narrows each of its rows. The selftests cover a directory narrowed to a file, an id nobody holds refused, an entry outside the taken set refused, a widening back refused when another hold meets it and allowed when none does, and a fill that offers a row the narrowed hold no longer meets though the taken one did. Record what was built as a new subsection of §424. §424.3 §230.3
